description: BESM (Brazilian Earth System Model) is the coupled Earth System Model developed at INPE/CPTEC (Brazil), used for seasonal-to-decadal prediction and for climate change projections, with contributions to CMIP5, CMIP6, and ongoing preparation for CMIP7 (including HighResMIP2).  **Scientific focus and approach**  BESM targets global coupled climate simulation and projection, spanning seasonal-to decadal prediction and multi-decadal/centennial climate change scenarios, with emphasis on tropical Atlantic and South American climate variability.  **Common code base and physics**  All family members couple the Brazilian Atmospheric Model (**BAM**) to the GFDL ocean model **MOM6** via the **FMS** coupler, with the GFDL sea ice model **SIS2**. Land surface is represented by **IBIS** in this configuration (SSiB is available in the coupling infrastructure but not used here; the COBALT ocean biogeochemistry model is likewise available but not active in this configuration).  **How family members differ**  Members differ mainly in atmosphere/ocean horizontal and vertical resolution and in the forcing/scenario configuration used — e.g. BESM-OA2.5 (CMIP5-era configuration) versus the current BESM3.0 configuration being prepared for CMIP7.
